events.title: Pope Gregory XI returns the papacy to Rome
events.description: Urged on by Catherine of Siena, Gregory XI entered Rome, ending almost seven decades in which the popes had lived at Avignon. His death the next year set off the Great Western Schism.
events.html: Urged on by Catherine of Siena, Gregory XI entered Rome, ending almost seven decades in which the popes had lived at Avignon. His death the next year set off the Great Western Schism.

events.title: James Cook makes the first recorded crossing of the Antarctic Circle
events.description: HMS Resolution and HMS Adventure sailed south of 66°33' S, the first ships known to do so. Cook's voyage showed that any southern continent must lie far to the south, beyond the pack ice.
events.html: HMS Resolution and HMS Adventure sailed south of 66°33' S, the first ships known to do so. Cook's voyage showed that any southern continent must lie far to the south, beyond the pack ice.

events.title: Daniel Morgan routs Tarleton at the Battle of Cowpens
events.description: In South Carolina, Daniel Morgan's Continentals and militia destroyed Banastre Tarleton's British force with a skilful double envelopment. The victory was a turning point in the southern campaign.
events.html: In South Carolina, Daniel Morgan's Continentals and militia destroyed Banastre Tarleton's British force with a skilful double envelopment. The victory was a turning point in the southern campaign.

events.title: Hawaii's Queen Liliuokalani overthrown
events.description: A committee of American and European businessmen, supported by US Marines from the USS Boston, deposed the Hawaiian queen and set up a provisional government. The United States annexed Hawaii in 1898.
events.html: A committee of American and European businessmen, supported by US Marines from the USS Boston, deposed the Hawaiian queen and set up a provisional government. The United States annexed Hawaii in 1898.

events.title: Soviet and Polish troops enter the ruins of Warsaw
events.description: The Red Army and the Polish First Army took Warsaw, abandoned by the Germans. After the crushing of the 1944 Uprising, the Germans had systematically razed the city, destroying about 85 per cent of it.
events.html: The Red Army and the Polish First Army took Warsaw, abandoned by the Germans. After the crushing of the 1944 Uprising, the Germans had systematically razed the city, destroying about 85 per cent of it.

events.title: UN Security Council meets for the first time
events.description: The United Nations Security Council held its first session at Church House, Westminster. Its five permanent members, each with a veto, were the United States, the Soviet Union, Britain, France and China.
events.html: The United Nations Security Council held its first session at Church House, Westminster. Its five permanent members, each with a veto, were the United States, the Soviet Union, Britain, France and China.

events.title: Eisenhower warns of the 'military-industrial complex'
events.description: In his televised farewell address, the outgoing President cautioned that a permanent arms industry and huge defence establishment could acquire 'unwarranted influence' over American government.
events.html: In his televised farewell address, the outgoing President cautioned that a permanent arms industry and huge defence establishment could acquire 'unwarranted influence' over American government.

events.title: Operation Desert Storm opens with air strikes on Iraq
events.description: A US-led coalition began a massive air campaign against Iraq, which had occupied Kuwait since August 1990. A ground offensive in late February expelled Iraqi forces within 100 hours.
events.html: A US-led coalition began a massive air campaign against Iraq, which had occupied Kuwait since August 1990. A ground offensive in late February expelled Iraqi forces within 100 hours.

events.title: Great Hanshin earthquake devastates Kobe
events.description: A magnitude 6.9 earthquake struck the Kobe region before dawn, killing 6,434 people and destroying over 100,000 buildings. The slow official response prompted reform of Japan's disaster planning.
events.html: A magnitude 6.9 earthquake struck the Kobe region before dawn, killing 6,434 people and destroying over 100,000 buildings. The slow official response prompted reform of Japan's disaster planning.
